title: Slush frozen drink, no sugar added

content.title: About
content.content: Slush is a frozen beverage made from water, natural fruit extracts and flavorings, prepared without added sugar. It has a light, refreshing texture and a vivid taste achieved through concentrated fruit essences.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Slush is often served at summer cafés and festivals as an alternative to carbonated drinks.
The lack of sugar makes it suitable for people monitoring blood glucose levels.
Flavor can be enhanced with natural sweeteners such as stevia, but the basic version contains none.
The freezing process retains most of the vitamins and antioxidants present in the fruit extracts.
Slush can be made at home using frozen water and flavorings.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: High water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Absence of sugar makes the drink low‑calorie, which is convenient for weight management.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Fruit extracts may provide vitamin C and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: No artificial colors
items.content: Most versions use only natural color derived from fruits.

items.title: Artificial flavorings
items.content: Some formulations may contain synthetic flavorings that could trigger sensitivity in certain individuals.

items.title: Cold shock
items.content: Consuming very cold drinks can cause discomfort in teeth or throat for sensitive people.

items.title: Allergy to fruit extracts
items.content: People with known fruit allergies should check the ingredient list before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sugar‑free slush in a glass or cup; you can add a lemon slice or mint for extra freshness. It is best enjoyed slowly, allowing it to melt and release its aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen slush in an airtight container in the freezer at –18 °C. Over time ice crystals may form, so slightly thaw before serving.
